Each configured parameter carries LOB, limit/premium band, permitted geography/class, referral trigger and effective date, and maps 1:1 to the signed Binding Authority Agreement schedule; any parameter without a BAA source clause is not saved.
The count and values of configured parameters reconcile to the BAA authority schedule; a four-eyes check confirms every schedule line is represented in the system (delta 0).

Configuration screenshots and the parameter mapping sheet are saved to SharePoint /DelegatedAuthority/Coverholders/<coverholder-id>/setup/authority-config-v1 with timestamp and version, retained for the life of the binder plus 7 years.
Any mismatch between the BAA and the configured parameter is logged in Archer GRC and corrected before the binder is activated; go-live is blocked until 0 open configuration exceptions.

checklist.step: Configure clear authority levels by premium, limit and line of business
checklist.value: PolicyCenter authority parameters set to enforce the BAA limits per LOB, premium band and geography.

testing.step: Verify configured limits match the agreement
testing.value: Four-eyes check confirms every configured limit ties to the BAA schedule; 0 mismatches before activation.

checklist.step: Configure documented referral triggers in the system
checklist.value: Referral rules (limit breach, restricted class, aggregation) configured so out-of-authority risks are auto-referred.

testing.value: Test transactions confirm each configured trigger fires and routes correctly; 0 triggers failing to fire.

checklist.step: Restrict binding to authorised users and within the configured caps
checklist.value: System roles and caps set so only authorised coverholder profiles can bind within the delegated limits.

testing.value: Attempted over-limit or unauthorised binds are blocked in test; 0 unauthorised binds possible.

answers.value: The claims-handling authority and TPA arrangements for a coverholder binder - settlement-authority limits, reserve authority, claims-reporting thresholds, TPA scope, complaint handling and audit rights - documented in the Binding Authority Agreement and TPA schedule.
Effective from the binder/TPA appointment date (e.g. 2026-07-01), reviewed at each renewal; reporting thresholds apply to claims arising on or after that date.

The arrangement records settlement-authority caps by LOB, reserve-authority limit, large-loss reporting threshold, TPA scope and audit rights; a schedule missing the reporting threshold or audit-rights clause is not finalized.
Documented authority caps and thresholds reconcile to the underwriting appetite and the reinsurance/treaty reporting requirements; the TPA scope matches the licensed lines (delta 0 against the BAA).

The signed claims-authority schedule and TPA agreement are saved to SharePoint /DelegatedAuthority/Coverholders/<coverholder-id>/setup/claims-authority-v1 and the executed contract in the contract repository, retained for the life of the binder plus 7 years.
Open points (e.g. undefined threshold, missing audit clause) are logged in Archer GRC and closed before the arrangement goes live; the binder cannot activate claims authority with open exceptions.
Sample claims-authority parameters trace back to the signed BAA/TPA schedule clauses to confirm the documented caps and thresholds match the executed contract.
Claim status and reporting-trigger fields in ClaimCenter align to the defined reporting thresholds so large losses are escalated per the arrangement.
Reporting-deadline and review dates align to the contract terms (e.g. large loss reported within 5 business days of the coverholder becoming aware).
The full claims-authority schedule and TPA arrangement for the binder (census of clauses), validated against the executed contract and appetite.

PASS = every claims-authority cap, reporting threshold, TPA scope and audit right is documented and consistent with the contract and appetite. FAIL = any undefined cap/threshold or missing audit/reporting clause.
On FAIL, hold finalization, log the gap in Archer GRC, obtain the missing clause or approval, and re-review before activation.

The delegation matrix records that claims settlement above the delegated cap reverts to the carrier's Claims Director/Manager and that TPA appointment/scope changes require Delegated Authority Manager and Legal sign-off.

Materiality/tolerance thresholds: settlement-authority cap per LOB, reserve-authority limit, and the large-loss reporting threshold (e.g. any claim >USD 100k or any coverage dispute) that obliges the coverholder/TPA to notify the carrier.

Field definitions (settlement_cap, reserve_authority, reporting_threshold, tpa_scope, audit_rights) come from the claims-authority schedule; control totals reconcile the documented caps to the underwriting appetite and treaty reporting requirements.
